subject: SIG: separation controls, deployment-mode evidence & delivery plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmecorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG: separation controls, deployment-mode evidence & delivery plan

Hi Lena —

Thanks for sending the SIG starter questionnaire. To speed review on our side I wanted to outline the specific artifacts we can provide that map to the "deployment modes" questions (Hosted / Dedicated / Private-VPC / On‑prem) and propose a short delivery plan.

TL;DR — what we can provide immediately:
- Hosted: architecture diagram, multi-tenant isolation matrix, SOC 2 report excerpt, default encryption-at-rest details.
- Dedicated: tenancy matrix (customer-dedicated GPU pools), network boundary diagram, sample tenant on-boarding checklist.
- Private (VPC / on‑prem): VPC peering / transit architecture, customer-managed KMS integration notes, and evidence of on-prem packaging/installation checklist.

Attachments I will push to the shared folder: redwood-hosted-arch.svg (diagram), dedicated-tenancy-matrix.xlsx (table), redwood-soc2-report-2026.pdf (certified report).

Proposed short plan:
1) Today: high-level diagrams + list of artifacts (this thread).
2) Tue (48h): Karthik to drop KMS/RBAC evidence for Dedicated & Private.
3) Wed: Marissa to prepare tenant isolation test plan and exportable logs examples.
4) Thu: assemble a SIG-ready artifact bundle and a one-page mapping doc that points each SIG question to the artifact.

If that timeline works for you, we will upload the files to the shared Drive link below and flag any redlines you want us to consider (e.g., additional contractual language around data residency).

Shared link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/ACME/SIG-evidence-pack

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]
[Attachment: redwood-hosted-arch.svg (image/svg+xml)]
[Attachment: dedicated-tenancy-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmecorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acmecorp.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: separation controls, deployment-mode evidence & delivery plan

Thanks Jordan — very helpful summary. A couple of clarifying asks before we sync the security review board:

1) For Hosted: can you confirm whether tenant isolation is logical (namespaces + runtime tagging) or also backed by hardware affinity in any cases? If logical, please include any noisy-neighbor mitigation controls and SLOs for noisy-tenant detection.

2) For Dedicated: we need a sample network diagram that includes S3/Blob access paths, any NAT/GW components, and whether customer traffic traverses shared control plane hops.

3) For Private/VPC: we will want evidence that customer-managed KMS is supported end-to-end (client-initiated CMKs, rotation logs, HSM-backed references). A screenshot or export of a successful KMS-attach test and the VPC peering config would be ideal.

Last: please include the contract appendix language you mentioned that guarantees deletion/backup retention for Dedicated and Private installs — our legal team requires specific SLA language to proceed.

Can you deliver the items above by Thu EOD?

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Senior Security Program Manager — Acme Corp
[lena.ortiz@acmecorp.com]

Karthik — can you assemble the Dedicated & Private artifacts Lena requests (network diagrams that show S3/Blob paths and control-plane hops; KMS attach test export; rotation logs sample). Attach any HSM/KMS architecture notes. Please add redwood-soc2-report-2026.pdf if helpful.

Marissa — can you draft the tenant isolation test plan for Hosted (noisy‑neighbor detection, tagging, runtime limits) and produce a short contract appendix snippet for deletion/retention language that Legal can review?

Target: Thu EOD deliverable to Lena. If any item needs more time, flag now.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SIG: separation controls, deployment-mode evidence & delivery plan

Jordan / Marissa / Lena — quick update from infra: we have the initial artifacts ready and have uploaded to the Drive link. Highlights: 

- redwood-soc2-report-2026.pdf (redacted PII sections) — covers control mapping for encryption and logical separation.
- redwood-hosted-arch.svg — shows namespace isolation, runtime tagging, and noisy‑neighbor throttling paths; notes that hosted uses logical isolation only (no explicit hardware affinity) but customers with high isolation requirements are routed to Dedicated or Private buckets by policy.
- dedicated-tenancy-matrix.xlsx — includes network path columns (S3/Blob, control-plane hops, NAT/GW) and a sample VPC layout.
- vpc-deployment-checklist.pdf — step-by-step for VPC peering and KMS attach test; includes an example rotation log export (redacted).

Attachments in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/ACME/SIG-evidence-pack (same link)

Notes on contractual language: Marissa will send a draft appendix. For the KMS proof: the export is a CSV of the rotation events (anonymized) and a screenshot of a successful KMS attach is in the folder. If Acme needs HSM attestation we can coordinate a short call with the infra team.

ETA: if you confirm receipt and that the artifacts match the ask I will mark this as delivered and we can run a quick readout with your security reviewers.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-soc2-report-2026.pdf (application/pdf)]
